actualUpstreamBothRigidComparison.driverInternalCurrentRegulation: A regulated current driver still needs its own current measurement. It is not an outer-controller telemetry channel in these runs.

controller.strategy: Nine-state sampled disturbance observer with discrete LQI feedback, true-contact-force integral feedback and estimated-friction compensation
controller.scalarFeedbackLaw: i_request = I_hold + currentFeedback*(i_hat-I_hold) + accelerationFeedback*aS_hat + friction_hat/Kf + integralGain*integral(F_reference-F_contact_hat), before current limiting and antiwindup.
controller.comparisonInterpretation: The observer estimates the physical contact force and disturbances; LQI supplies feedback gains. Direct raw-cell PI/PID regulates a different force quantity. Its failed true-contact-force tests do not prove that PI/PID laws with an inertial estimator cannot work.

actualUpstreamBothRigidComparison.gateInterpretation: Corrected estimated contact force gates slow recentering; recenter travel comes from inferred gap. All4clean corners exercise recenter (ready86.284%,4opens each; max added request2.475 mm/s). All16noisy corners gateReady0, so those qualify fast control and bounded nominal robot motion, not active noisy recenter.
actualUpstreamBothRigidComparison.extraUnknownDelayFailure: An extra unmodeled100 us force delay loses contact by0.0027 s at50 N/90° seed7, before the bump/robot command with gateReady0. This is a fast-loop timing failure, not recenter feedback.

actualUpstreamBothRigidComparison.thermalObservation: At50 N/90° the nominal trace has approximately2.5 A RMS and25 W copper loss for4 ohm. Temperature rise, continuous rating and cooling are not simulated.
actualUpstreamBothRigidComparison.qualificationLimits: Four corners and four finite noise seeds, exact matched plant/controller masses, force constant, current timing and Coulomb model; this is not a hardware qualification or a proof over arbitrary noise/jitter/model errors.
actualUpstreamBothRigidComparison.conclusion: The corrected both-rigid observer is the best nominal actual-sensor controller found in this lane. It passes the stated noisy corner tests with about0.074 N margin, but calibrated latency/gain/mass/bias requirements must be demonstrated before using it as a physical-prototype recommendation.
actualUpstreamBothRigidComparison.rigidPositionSensorEquivalence: With both rigid links, moving B and tool S have the same displacement. Therefore S-A equals minus the actuator A-B gap up to its static offset; the original internal coil/magnet position sensor can provide the same information if it meets the qualified timing/noise specification. This equivalence does not generally hold for compliant B/S mechanics.

boundedCurrentUncertaintyStudy.conclusion: Adding current-state process uncertainty or a random-walk actuator-force state did not qualify +/-0.1% unknown Kf across both seeds. Nominal calibrated performance remains a conditional result.
